graph.title: Billund Airport
notes: The manual is pictures only; exact stud-to-stud positions are inferred from the isometric views, so many joins use null ports or approximate studs, and which baseplate or lower piece a part sits on is a best reading.
The four 6x12 base plates (b1, b7, b10, b13) are held together only by the black tiles bridging their edges. Each plate is joined to the tiles that overhang it.

Parts in the 'repeats' groups (gate x5, wing x4, blk x3, tw x2, stk x2, rp x2, fa x4, fb x4, plane x5) count towards the 286-piece inventory. Together with b1-b187 they total 286 pieces and match the colour/type counts in the parts list.
Gate (step 17): a trans-clear 1x2 plate on each of the five tan 1x2 plates, with a LBG 1x1 tile on one stud. Each plane (step 50) is joined to the free stud of the matching gate plate.
Wing (step 19) units are placed on jumpers 2-5 (b24-b27). The step 32 unit (b122-b129) goes on jumper 1 (b23).

Planes: five identical builds with colour overrides. The tail slope and wing tile are modelled as stacked on the coloured 1x2 plate; the clear cockpit slope sits on the third stud of the white 1x3 plate.

Flower 24866 is modelled with a top attachment (null port) because the real part has a top stud but the catalogue lists only anti.1.1. Blue round plate + green flower stacks and orange flower + white round plate stacks are assumed.
The flag pole (87994 bar) is assumed to stand in a stud of green plate b70. The clip b182 grips the bar (clip/bar, revolute).
Step 43 tower is read as clear 1x2 pair, white 2x2, clear 1x2 pair, white 2x2, clear 1x2, curved 2x2 on top. It is attached to white plate b94.
Cheese slopes (54200) are joined by their stud on the top face; the clear slope in step 27 attaches to the SNOT brick's side stud.
